init.title: Options
init.description: Brew detection and the auto-stop switch, or the bean profiles. A bean profile stores a target ratio per bean: choose the bean with the entity 'Bean' and the target ratio follows; changing 'Target ratio' while a bean is active updates its profile.

detection.title: Brew detection
detection.description: A brew is the time the scale's timer runs, plus a short capture tail for the drips. The dose is detected automatically from weighing the beans before the brew. All values below have sensible defaults; change them only if brews are missed, split, or saved with a wrong dose. Optional: a stop switch for the adaptive auto-stop. Bean profiles are in their own menu entries.

data.tail_seconds: Extra weighing after the weight is calm

data_description.tail_seconds: With the auto-stop: after the cut the scale's timer keeps running until the weight is calm, then this much longer for late drops; then the timer is stopped and the weight at that moment is the yield (and what the auto-stop learns from). Lifting the cup ends it at once. Without the auto-stop (timer stopped by hand or by the scale) recording also goes on for this long after the timer stop, but the paused scale sends no weight, so drops after the stop are not counted: stop the timer only once the drips are in.
data_description.min_duration: Timer runs shorter than this are not saved as brews, e.g. a quick flush or an accidental timer start.
data_description.min_yield: Runs that end with less than this in the cup are not saved as brews, e.g. the timer ran without coffee.
data_description.dose_min: How the dose is found: put the dosing cup or portafilter on the scale, tare, add the beans. The last weight that stays stable inside this range before the brew counts as the dose. Set the range around your usual dose (default 12–25 g).
data_description.dose_max: Upper end of the dose range (see above). Heavier stable weights, e.g. a full cup, are not taken as the dose.
data_description.stability_tolerance: How much the weight may wobble and still count as stable when detecting the dose.
data_description.stability_seconds: How long the weight has to stay stable to count as the dose.
data_description.dose_lookback_minutes: Only weight plateaus this recent before the brew can become its dose; older ones are ignored.
data_description.stop_switch: Optional. A switch that ends the shot when turned off, usually the smart plug of the espresso machine. During a brew the integration turns it off early enough that the cup ends on the target once the drips have settled, and learns the machine's delay and drip from every shot. Set the target with the entities 'Target ratio' (ratio × detected dose) or 'Target yield' (fixed grams, also used when no dose was detected). Leave empty to disable the auto-stop.
data_description.pump_power: Optional, experimental. A number entity that sets the pump power (e.g. a phase or pulse-skip dimmer in the pump circuit). Its range (min to max) is used as 0-100 %. With it and the stop switch, the pump throttle can slow down a shot that would end too early (entity 'Pump throttle': off, observe, throttle). The pump must fall back to full power on its own when Home Assistant is unreachable. Leave empty if your machine has no such control: the throttle then only observes.

add_bean.title: Add bean profile
add_bean.description: A bean profile remembers the target ratio for one coffee. The auto-stop keeps learning one shared model for all beans; the bean only labels the brews.

data_description.name: Shown in the entity 'Bean', in the brew card and saved with every brew made while it is active. Must be unique.
data_description.ratio: Yield / dose for this bean with the pump profile below (Standard without one), e.g. 2.0 for 18 g in, 36 g out. The bean keeps a ratio per pump profile: its ratios for other profiles stay. Selecting the bean sets the target ratio of the auto-stop to it.
data_description.note: Optional, for yourself (roaster, roast date, grind setting).
data_description.shot_time: Optional. Target shot time of the pump throttle for this bean (pump on to pump off). Empty: the global 'Target shot time'.
data_description.profile: Optional. Selecting this bean also selects this pump profile; choosing another profile while the bean is active makes that one the bean's. Empty: the active profile stays until one is chosen.

delete_bean.description: Stored brews keep the bean name. If the deleted bean is active, the newest remaining bean becomes active and its ratio the target; after the last one no bean is active (the target ratio stays).

delete_brew.name: Delete brew
delete_brew.description: Removes a stored brew from the history and takes its sample out of the auto-stop learning (the model is recomputed from the remaining samples). Brew count and coffee total are totals of all brews made and are not reduced. Returns the brew ID, whether it was in the learning and the model afterwards.

entry_id.name: Scale
entry_id.description: Config entry of the scale. Optional with a single scale.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Scale device (instead of the config entry).

brew_id.name: Brew ID
brew_id.description: ID of a stored brew (websocket difluid_scale/brews, brew completed event).

learn_stop_from_brew.name: Learn stop from brew
learn_stop_from_brew.description: Feeds a past brew into the auto-stop model: weight and weight-derived flow at the cut time from the stored profile, overshoot = stored yield - weight at cut. Same acceptance checks as a live sample. Returns the computed sample. If the brew's sample is still in the learning journal (the last 50 samples), it is replaced instead of counted twice.

entry_id.name: Scale
entry_id.description: Config entry of the scale. Optional with a single scale.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Scale device (instead of the config entry).

brew_id.name: Brew ID
brew_id.description: ID of a stored brew (websocket difluid_scale/brews, brew completed event).

cut_offset.name: Cut time
cut_offset.description: Seconds from the brew start at which the stop switch was turned off.

target.name: Target yield
target.description: Optional: target of that brew; only used for the deviation in the response.

switch_latency.name: Switch latency
switch_latency.description: Optional: seconds from the turn_off call to the stop switch reporting off for that cut (e.g. from the recorder). Overrides the latency stored with the brew. With a latency the sample is corrected to the nominal switch latency like a live cut. A brew whose measurement ended without a value is not learned unless this is given; brews from before 0.5.1 (never measured) are learned uncorrected.

add_bean.description: Adds a bean profile (name, target ratio, note) like the options do, without reloading the integration; usable from a dashboard.

ratio.name: Target ratio
ratio.description: Yield / dose, 0.5–5, for the bean's pump profile (Standard without one). Empty: the current target ratio of the scale.

note.name: Note

shot_time.name: Target shot time
shot_time.description: Optional: target shot time of the pump throttle for this bean (s). Empty: the global one.

profile.name: Pump profile

activate.name: Activate
activate.description: Make it the active bean right away, so the target ratio follows (default: on). The first bean is always activated.

stop_switch_unavailable.title: Stop switch of {name} could not be used
stop_switch_unavailable.description: The auto-stop of {name} uses the switch `{entity_id}`, but it does not exist, or it was missing or unavailable when the auto-stop tried to switch the machine off, so brews are not stopped at the target. A switch that only becomes unavailable while the machine is off (e.g. a relay powered from the same socket) is not reported. Make the switch available again or choose another one (or none) under Settings > Devices & services > DiFluid Microbalance > Configure > Brew detection and stop switch. This message disappears by itself once the switch is back.

stop_switch_latency_unknown.title: Stop switch of {name} does not report off in time
stop_switch_latency_unknown.description: The auto-stop of {name} turns off `{entity_id}`, but at the last {count} auto-stops in a row the switch did not report `off` within 5 seconds (or the call failed). Without that report the switch's delay cannot be separated from the drip, so these shots were not learned and the auto-stop no longer adapts. Check the switch's connection (e.g. Zigbee signal, MQTT reporting) or choose another switch under Settings > Devices & services > DiFluid Microbalance > Configure > Brew detection and stop switch. This message disappears by itself at the next auto-stop with a measured latency.

profile_bloom_scale_auto_stop.title: Pump profile {profile} of {name}: turn off the scale's auto stop timing
profile_bloom_scale_auto_stop.description: The active pump profile {profile} has a phase with the pump off (0 %, a bloom), and the scale's own *Auto stop timing* is on. The scale may stop its timer while no coffee flows, which ends the brew – and with it the auto-stop – in the middle of the shot. Turn off the switch *Auto stop timing* of {name}, or choose a profile without a 0 % phase. This message disappears by itself.

profile_bloom_pump_min.title: Pump profile {profile} of {name}: the pump cannot be switched off
profile_bloom_pump_min.description: The active pump profile {profile} has a phase with the pump off (0 %, a bloom), but the pump power entity `{entity_id}` cannot go below {min} (its minimum). That phase runs at the minimum instead – a slow preinfusion, not a bloom. Allow 0 on the pump entity (e.g. in its ESPHome configuration) or choose a profile without a 0 % phase. This message disappears by itself.

auto_stop_cut_failed.title: Auto-stop of {name} could not switch the machine off
auto_stop_cut_failed.description: The auto-stop of {name} tried {attempts} times within 2 minutes to turn off `{entity_id}` and failed every time, so the shot may have run on. Check the switch (connection, power) and turn the machine off by hand if it still runs. This message disappears when the switch reports off or at the next successful auto-stop.

auto_stop_cut_failed_retrying.title: Auto-stop of {name} cannot switch the machine off
auto_stop_cut_failed_retrying.description: The auto-stop of {name} could not turn off `{entity_id}` at the target, so the shot may be running on: check the machine now and turn it off by hand if needed. It keeps trying for 2 minutes, and at once when the switch is reachable again. This message disappears when the switch reports off or the auto-stop succeeds.

auto_stop_cut_failed_pump.title: Auto-stop of {name} could not switch the machine off
auto_stop_cut_failed_pump.description: The auto-stop of {name} tried {attempts} times within 2 minutes to turn off `{entity_id}` and failed every time, so the shot may have run on. The pump power was set back to full power. Check the switch (connection, power) and turn the machine off by hand if it still runs. This message disappears when the switch reports off or at the next successful auto-stop.
